title: Action-Only Monitoring as Sufficient Baseline: When Does CoT Not Help?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly informs monitoring resource allocation: knowing which task types don't benefit from CoT monitoring saves compute and simplifies deployment. Practical and actionable.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: METR public tasks are available on GitHub. Requires setting up both CoT and action-only monitors across multiple task types. The pipeline setup is the main complexity, but each comparison is straightforward once built.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple task types (coding, web browsing, file manipulation) each needing both monitor conditions. The task-type ranking is a clear deliverable, but covering enough types for meaningful ranking stretches the 30-hour budget.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
